recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-5280 unless OO reopens the broader Request/Task workflow distinction; the Order-specific clarification was applied and then intentionally superseded by the current workflow model.
issue_request: FHIR-5280 was a Published OO DSTU1 ballot issue with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. It declined moving Order into the clinical resource list and instead required an Order introduction Boundaries section explaining that Order is a workflow resource, not a clinical resource, used to manage fulfillment requests and state transitions for the real clinical order resources.
initial_application: Commit d6259fa8e3beda8fd5e58ad54d85001f1efb9d42 included '[#5280] X added boundaries section to Order' and added the requested Boundaries and Relationships paragraph to source/order/order-introduction.xml, so the seed had a concrete initial source application.
additional_context: Later Published OO workflow decisions superseded the old target. FHIR-10059 removed Order and OrderResponse because Task superseded their scope and function, and commit 16997a29cae89d6a31d09dabd782afdb0077b2e7 removed Order/OrderResponse from fhir.ini and deleted the Order source. FHIR-10295 renamed order resources to Request resources because the same structures represent proposals, plans, recommendations, and orders. Current source/fhir.ini lists Order, DiagnosticOrder, and DiagnosticRequest as deleted/renamed resources, while ServiceRequest and Task are active.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Editing deleted Order source would be out of build scope, and re-adding the 2015 wording to current ServiceRequest or Task pages would duplicate existing Request-pattern, ServiceRequest, and Task guidance that already separates request authorization/intention from fulfillment and execution tracking.
